# Zoop Internet

> Zoop Internet is an open-source direct device-to-device mesh platform that lets trusted devices share internet securely without routing payload through centralized VPN servers. Built on WireGuard (ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519), STUN/TURN NAT traversal, and Ed25519 identities.

- **Website:** https://zoopinternet.online
- **GitHub:** https://github.com/zoop-internet/zoop
- **Docs:** https://zoopinternet.online/how-it-works
- **Downloads:** https://zoopinternet.online/downloads
- **Security:** https://zoopinternet.online/security
- **API docs:** https://github.com/zoop-internet/zoop/blob/main/docs/api.md

## What Zoop Does
- Provider endpoints (home broadband, phone hotspot, office) share connectivity with Recipient endpoints (laptop on road, family device) via direct encrypted tunnels.
- Control Plane (identity, auth, signaling, IPAM 100.64.0.0/10) coordinates; Data Plane carries traffic directly (preferred) or via relay fallback.
- Daemon `zoopd` manages TUN/WireGuard; CLI `zoop` manages via Unix socket; Cloud `zoop-cloud` is coordinator.

## Why Not a VPN?
- No centralized payload routing; lower latency; end-to-end encrypted; zero-knowledge relays; roaming (Wi-Fi↔cellular) via Netlink.

## Quick Start
```bash
make build
./bin/zoop-cloud
sudo ./bin/zoopd -tun zoop0 -api-port 9090
zoop status && zoop connect <peer-id>
```

## FAQ

**Q: What is Zoop?** A: Direct device-to-device internet sharing mesh, open-source, WireGuard-encrypted.

**Q: How is it different from a VPN?** A: Payload goes directly device-to-device, not via company servers—faster and more private.

**Q: Is traffic private?** A: Yes, end-to-end encrypted; control plane and relays cannot decrypt.

**Q: Does it work behind NAT/CGNAT?** A: Yes, via STUN discovery (host + srflx candidates), UDP hole punching, relay fallback.

**Q: What platforms?** A: Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, OpenWrt.

**Q: What is the Zoop ID?** A: Permanent identity `ZP-XXXXXX` (6-char alphabet 23456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ) plus mutable @username; PIN is 6 digits.

**Q: Is it free?** A: Yes, MIT-licensed. Self-hostable control plane.
